title: serving-runtime-scratchpad-samira
content:
2026-03-13 | daily scratchpad (serving-runtime)
---
Quick context: triaging a regression where small-context requests (<=32 tokens) see p95 jump after the continuous-batching change + new fused-kernel selection. Repro is flaky locally; seems load-dependent. Notes / steps / quick todos below.

Morning triage:
- Symptoms: p50 ~ stable, p95 for 8-token completions moved from ~28ms -> ~42ms on g4dn.xlarge tests. Tail only on hosted API (high QPS).
- Initial suspicion: batching policy + kv-cache interaction causing extra memcpy + small-batch kernel mismatch.
- High-level theory: for short sequences we are using fused-attn-v2 (fast for medium seq) but that kernel forces an extra host->device memcpy when KV cache hits cause broken alignment for some models (llama-variant). When batching mixes requests with and without KV, runtime inserts fallback path.

Repro steps I used (local):
- Start minimal local stack: docker-compose -f dev-compose.yml up serving redis
- Cmd to run microbench: python infra/bench/latency.py --model redwood/llama-13b-small --batch-size 16 --concurrency 8 --seq 8 --requests 2000  # note: use --warmup 200
- Observed: 95th latency ~40ms with fused-attn enabled, ~26ms with fused-attn disabled
- Metric collection: ./tools/collect-trace.sh --pid $(pgrep runtime) -> nvprof / nvtx traces looked like memcpy spikes at start-of-request for a subset of requests

Immediate experiments to run (priority order):
- [ ] Reproduce under controlled QPS with and without kv-cache enabled for same trace file (use bench harness to toggle caching)
- [ ] Force kernel selection override to fused-attn-v1 for seq<=64, measure p95 delta (A/B)
- [ ] Add micro-benchmark that simulates mixed KV/no-KV batch to reproduce memcpy path
- [ ] Test new continuous-batcher changes with batching.window=5ms and 1ms to see SLO impact

Notes on kernel behavior:
- fused-attn-v2: excellent for seq 128-512, uses split-kv layout optimization, but requires aligned paddings. If request has active KV cache (non-zero past length), code path attempts to concat and then uses an extra device buffer -> extra memcpy in fast path.
- fallback kernel (generic): lower perf but avoids memcpy for small seq. Under mixed batches runtime picks fused-v2 and then serializes the small-seq requests resulting in higher queuing latency.

Perf numbers (local raw runs):
- baseline (no fused): p50=11.2ms p95=26.7ms throughput=380rps (seq=8, batch=16)
- fused-v2 enabled: p50=9.5ms p95=41.8ms throughput=410rps
- fused-v1 forced: p50=10.1ms p95=28.0ms throughput=390rps
-> observation: fused-v2 improves median but inflates tail when requests are mixed.

Kernel selection TODOs:
- Add heuristic: if batch contains >20% requests with active KV cache and seq < 64 -> prefer v1/generic kernel (avoid extra memcpy).
- Add metrics: kernel_choice, kernel_memcpy_bytes, per-request memcpy time in traces (NVTX tags)
- Rollout plan: bake heuristic in dev, run canary on Dedicated pool with low traffic, monitor p95 and memcopy metric.

Bug triage items (INF-1290):
- Repro steps added to ticket (link above).
- Owners: assigned to @ethan (initial investigation), @samira (kernel heuristics patch & micro-bench)
- Suggested label: perf, kv-cache, regression-1.6.2
- Immediate mitigation: patch runtime to force fused-attn off for <64 sequences on hosted production as quick rollback (can be feature-flagged).

Short-term tactical checklist:
- [x] add NVTX markers around KV concat path (done local branch samira/kv-nvtx)
- [ ] instrument metrics to count memcpy events (samira/metric-memcpy)
- [ ] create bench-case that replays production request mix (need sample traces from hosted)
- [ ] sync with SRE before rolling any kernel defaults to prod (pinged @lina)

Notes for PRs / code pointers:
- probable change locations: runtime/kernels/selection.py, runtime/exec/batcher.cpp, runtime/exec/kv_cache.cpp
- local branch names I used: samira/kv-nvtx, samira/kernel-heuristic-v1
- quick test cmd: pytest -q tests/bench/test_kernel_selection.py -k mixed_kv

Kernel-specific micro-ideas:
- Avoid host memcpy by preallocating aligned device buffers per worker and use persistent streams for KV merges (reduces memcpy stalls). Risk: extra GPU memory usage + complexity on multi-tenant pools.
- Option: lazy KV concat — only concat for requests that will actually hit fused kernel; otherwise keep per-request small buffers and schedule them on generic kernel.

Longer-term experiments (Q2):
- Evaluate quantized fused kernels (4-bit) tradeoffs for short sequences; suspected improvement in memory copy overhead due to smaller buffer sizes.
- Measure effect of batched prefix caching: for repeated prefixes, we can serve many short queries via cache only path and avoid kernel selection entirely.
- Add a simulated load generator to reproduce interleaving patterns seen in production (CDF of past_lengths, seq_lengths) and feed into CI nightly to catch regressions.

Open questions / TODO to ask on call:
- Lina: do we have access to raw sample traces from last week (needed for bench)? (SLACK thread #prod-traces)
- Ethan: can we get a quick run of canary on a small Dedicated pool with kernel=forced-v1 for 24h?
- Infra: is there an easy flag to disable fused-attn via runtime config per-customer? If not, add feature flag surface.

Random commands / snippets (save here):
- Start perf harness: 
  docker-compose -f dev-compose.yml up -d redis postgres
  python infra/bench/latency.py --model redwood/llama-13b-small --concurrency 16 --batch-size 32 --seq 8 --requests 5000 --warmup 500 --kv-enabled

- Collect traces: 
  ./tools/collect-trace.sh --target runtime --duration 60 --out /tmp/trace.nvtx
  nvprof --profile-from-start off --session-name samira --output-profile /tmp/profile.nvprof -- ./runtime/bin/serving --config dev.yaml

- quick grep for memcpy path: 
  rg "memcpy" runtime -n || true

Meeting notes (sync 10:30):
- Quick status: reproduction confirmed, median ok, tail regressed.
- Action: patch heuristic -> run microbench -> canary -> metric dashboard update.
- Follow ups: Lina to get traces; Ethan to try mempool prealloc test; Samira to open kernel-heuristic PR by EOD.

Backlog + non-blocking ideas:
- Explore per-model kernel profiles persisted in catalog (model.profiles.kernel_preference) so we don't have to guess at runtime.
- Add canary rule: if tail increases >20% after kernel change, auto-roll back for that route.
- Look into lowering batching.window for small-seq routes to reduce mixing probability (cost: throughput).

Notes to self (personal):
- Keep PR small: expose config toggle and unit tests, then add telemetry in follow-up.
- Document experiment results in INF-1290 ticket with exact bench commands and seed for reproducibility.
- Double-check memory regression on night runs (leak risk with prealloc).

End of day deliverables (EOD):
- [ ] Open PR: samira/kernel-heuristic-v1 (small, with feature-flag + unit test)
- [ ] Upload bench traces to ticket INF-1290
- [ ] Post short summary to #runtime-perf channel: TL;DR + mitigation plan

-- SAMIRA
